change: Change only kWideBf16RetainedYRowAlignElems from 24 FP32 elements (96B row-span quantum) to 8 elements (32B). Init allocation padding, ChooseWideFullYRows budget padding, and ProcessWideLowPrecision retained-y indexing all derive from this constant. Slot phases, tile width, arithmetic, and synchronization are unchanged.
hypothesis: Reducing the retained-y row-span quantum to the existing 32B UB transfer-alignment granularity lowers or preserves per-row padding and changes row starts plus the following scratch-buffer base phases. This may improve, hurt, or be neutral for wide BF16 vector access. No physical UB bank mapping is inferred.

static_address_validation.row_stride_elems: round_up(rowWidth, 8); used consistently for valueFp32Buf_ allocation and both retained-y access passes.
static_address_validation.access_bound: For each batchRow < batchRows <= wideFullYRows_, tile col + valid <= rowWidth <= rowStrideElems. The highest accessed element is 16 + (batchRows - 1) * rowStrideElems + rowWidth - 1, strictly below 16 + wideFullYRows_ * rowStrideElems.
static_address_validation.relative_alignment: The retained-y phase is 64B, row stride is a multiple of 8 FP32 elements (32B), and full tile offsets are multiples of 4096 FP32 elements (16384B); all relative row/tile offsets preserve 32B alignment.
static_address_validation.budget: The same computed row padding is passed into ChooseWideFullYRows and used in InitBuffer allocation. For every supported wide width 8193..32768, alignment 8 has no more padding than alignment 24; simulated row-count/tile choices remain equal or improve. Canonical BF16 widths 16384 and 32768 keep their existing row/tile choices; budget footprints decrease by 32B and 64B respectively.
